title: Sparrow install fixes & env reminders
content:
Purpose / quick context:
- Field-day scratchpad for Sparrow (customer site) — capture small fixes, environment gotchas, and reminders for follow-up before the next install window.
- Not a polished runbook; written fast in the van between racks. Use for next-stage playbook updates.

Top-priority action items (follow-up before handoff):
- [ ] Confirm allowed egress to mirror registry (10.4.3.0/24) and open outbound 443 from nodes. Customer networking team must whitelist our jump box IP: 34.210.79.12.
- [ ] Get canonical LUKS passphrase escrow procedure approved by security (they want HSM-backed KMS, not plain file).
- [ ] Add MTU 9000 to Calico IP pool config (we saw jumbo frames enabled on switch).
- [ ] Swap: verify re-enable policy with SRE — we disabled swap for kube but customer wants swapfile present, need doc.

Hardware/environment notes (observed):
- Node inventory: 6x DGX-style boxes (512GB, 8xA100 80GB), 1x seed control VM behind customer firewall.
- Local NVMe layout: /dev/nvme0n1: root (LVM), /dev/nvme1n1: model disk (LUKS->xfs), /dev/sdb: spare.
- Observed SMART alert on host-3 nvme (attribute 5) — flagged to onsite tech for replacement.
- BIOS settings: C-state C6 disabled on 3/4 nodes (good), but host-5 had hyperthreading disabled — enabled and rebooted.

Network & DNS gotchas we hit:
- Systemd-resolved on jump box interfering with docker DNS resolution — bind /etc/resolv.conf to upstream 10.0.0.2 to avoid split-brain.
- Customer uses proxy for outbound and intercepts TLS. For airgapped install we need their internal registry cert (PEM) added to /etc/docker/certs.d/registry.internal:5000/ca.crt on each node.
- Kubernetes API VIP sits behind F5 with client cert auth. Bring client cert (sparrow-api-client.pem) and confirm CN mapping.
- MTU mismatch: nodes default 1500, infra team has data plane 9000; results in dropped packets during large-model pulls. We set node-level docker daemon.json {"mtu": 9000} and restarted dockerd.

Kernel / OS / runtime checks (commands & expected outcomes):
- disable swap: sudo swapoff -a && grep -v swap /etc/fstab || ensure kubelet has --fail-swap-on=false
- cgroups v2: sudo stat -f -c %T /sys/fs/cgroup -> should be cgroup2 (we prefer cgroup v2 for containerd on Ubuntu 22.04). On host-4 it returned "tmpfs" -> kernel boot missing systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1.
- nvidia driver: sudo systemctl status nvidia-persistenced -> expect active. Command we ran: nvidia-smi -L (should list 8 GPUs). On host-2 returned only 4 -> NVIDIA MIG partitioning misconfigured.
- docker vs containerd: team uses containerd. Verify: sudo crictl ps; sudo ctr images ls | grep redwood-models. If not present, pull via registry mirror.

Storage & encryption notes:
- LUKS header write: cryptsetup luksFormat /dev/nvme1n1 --type luks2; we used keyfile at /etc/cryptkeys/sparrow.key (must rotate).
- XFS mount options: noatime, nodiratime, reflink=0 (customer requested to avoid accidental reflink semantics).
- Model disk I/O scheduler switched to mq-deadline (from bfq) — benchmarked with fio and saw 8% perf gain for sequential writes.

Service & deployment quirks seen during smoke tests:
- KV cache warmup failed when prefix cache size set to 2GB on first start. Temporary fix: set cache_init_size=256MB then increase via rolling restart.
- Streaming endpoint fell back to CPU on overload (observed at ~1750 tokens/sec across cluster). Probable cause: runtime kernel OOM killer invoked for one pod. Need to pin oom_score_adj and resourceRequests for runtime.
- Canary rollout: our rollback hook didn't remove old model binary — left stale files on /opt/models. Add cleanup script to postRollback hook.

Useful commands I ran (paste these in playbook):
- check node GPUs: for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name); do kubectl debug -it $n --image=ubuntu -- bash -c "nvidia-smi -L || echo no-gpu"; done
- check containerd config: sudo cat /etc/containerd/config.toml | grep -nR "registry.mirrors" -n
- verify MTU: ip link show eth0 | grep mtu || ethtool -k eth0
- disk mapping: lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,MOUNTPOINT,UUID
- LUKS header backup: sudo cryptsetup luksHeaderBackup /dev/nvme1n1 --header-backup-file /tmp/luks-header-hostX.backup (copy to secure enclave)

Onsite human notes & contacts:
- Jack (on-site sysadmin) — good with rack work; keeps spare SATA-to-NVMe adapter in locker A3.
- Field windows: 9:00–15:00 local — customer prefers no reboots during peak 10:30–13:00.
- Slack channel created: #sparrow-field (add ops and sysadmin).

Open questions (needs decision):
- Use host-level NVMe encryption (LUKS) vs. filesystem-level encryption? Security prefers host-level; weigh perf impact.
- Customer wants a periodic snapshot schedule for models (rsync to warm-standby). Who owns restore runbook? Recommend Customer Success + Field Eng.
- KMS: do we store model keys in their HSM or our KMS gateway? Security is leaning to customer HSM for private deployments.

Small fixes to add to repo after return:
- deploy-scripts: add --mtu flag to node-bootstrap and documentation snippet for systemd-resolved workaround.
- add post-rollback cleanup for /opt/models (remove any files >7 days old unless pinned in models.json).
- update docs: note requirement for registry cert in airgap installs and a sample systemd unit for mounting LUKS keyfile at boot.

Quick timeline from today (what happened):
- 08:30: arrival, hardware inventory + BIOS checks.
- 09:20: addressed hyperthreading+reboot on host-5.
- 10:15: fixed docker DNS by replacing systemd-resolved symlink on jump box.
- 11:40: discovered nvme SMART warning on host-3; raised ticket with onsite tech (tracker CONF-4732).
- 14:00: smoke tests: streaming endpoint degraded -> raised incident and throttled canary.

If you take this next:
- Sync with Maya on LUKS escrow and write the short procedure (3 bullets) for security sign-off.
- Push the small deploy-scripts PR from linked_artifacts and include the MTU change.
- Create a concise one-page "Sparrow install TL;DR" for handoff to CS (1 page, bullet list).

Random tiny notes (for memory):
- Remember to return the SATA adapter to locker A3.
- Pack extra M6 bolts for the next rack move.

End of scratchpad — save to drive and convert two bullets into the spin-up checklist in the shared runbook repo.
